QUOTE: "**Default (no define):** external applications that include mbedtls headers. They cannot use the field names." and "**Opt-out:** the library itself and its own sample programs. Inside that code the field is accessed by its real name." plus the gate table showing `private_##m` (renamed) vs `m` (plain name).
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer explains that code defining MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS (library, samples) sees plain member names, while ordinary consumers of the public headers see the private_-renamed ones.
